tasks.short: Prepare from the referral, interview the client and family, write up the history, request records from other agencies and pass it to the social worker.

steps.what: Assistant reads the referral and the existing case file
Assistant asks the client's consent to record the interview and starts the recording
Assistant interviews the client and family members about their social, school, criminal and drug history
Assistant types up the interview from notes into the case file

loop.input: The interview recording, made only with the client's consent, and the case file's report headings.
loop.output: A draft history report under the headings, each paragraph linked to its time in the recording.
loop.check: A validator flags any statement about suicide, violence, abuse or drugs that does not appear in the transcript, and the assistant resolves every flag. The assistant reads each paragraph against the transcript, checks that it says what was said and nothing more, and approves it; nothing is written to the file without approval.
loop.stop: One draft per interview; on failure or refused consent the assistant writes from notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: The content is a free conversation; templates cannot turn it into a report.

steps.what: Client signs the consent for the records requests
Assistant prepares requests for records from schools, probation or other agencies in the secure-mail template
Assistant checks each request: records asked, the signed consent attached and the agency it goes to
Assistant sends the checked requests by secure mail
Social worker reviews the compiled history

tasks.design: With the client's consent the interview is recorded, and a bounded step drafts the history report in the case system ({OTHER}) with a validator that flags risk statements not in the transcript; the assistant approves before anything is saved; saving the history in the case file is an ordinary save, and the social worker reviews it there. Records requests use a secure-mail template with the client's consent attached; the interview itself stays as it is.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were typed from notes after each interview.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch social teams pilot drafting intake reports from recordings, with a worker checking every output and a DPIA done.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts have invented risk statements in reported cases, and summaries are weaker on multiple problems; many clients will not be recorded.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a family to tell the real story and noticing what they leave out.
tasks.altitude: The assistant approves drafts instead of typing; assessment stays with the social worker.

reach.learn: Whether the risk-statement validator flags invented content.

evidence.claim: A Dutch social team pilots recording intakes and drafting the report with language models, with a worker checking every output and a DPIA done.
In a UK council pilot with 20 children's social care staff, practitioners self-reported about 11 hours a week saved and 46% less weekly admin time.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation and irrelevant content in AI-drafted notes.
Recording staff conversations needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the social worker's review; assessment and decisions are outside.
Input contract: recording consent asked and stored by the assistant at the start; report headings set by the team; consent for records requests signed by the client; fallback is notes and typing.
Drafting runs under a processing agreement after a DPIA.

Social worker time and the client's consent signature (s3b) are outside the assistant's savings. About 70% of clients consent to recording; s3 is priced at that share. Checking and sending requests keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of clients who consent to recording.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a risk statement that was not said?

already_counted.description: Assistant checks the draft and resolves every validator flag.

incremental.description: No new focal work: asking consent is shown as step s1b.

approvals.approved_version: Each records request with the records asked for and the client's signed consent exactly as checked by the assistant in s4b, sent once by secure mail to the named agency; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of clients refuse recording or have many problems, so s3 keeps 65 (11.5); high: about 70% consent as assumed (15.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear what the client needs, find services on the social map, explain options, give an information sheet, refer with consent and follow up.

steps.what: Assistant listens to what the client needs
Assistant searches websites, folders and colleagues for suitable community services
Assistant explains the options and agrees the next step with the client
Assistant puts together an information sheet for the client
Assistant checks the information sheet: the service fits the client's need and its conditions and contacts are current
Assistant gives the checked information sheet to the client
Assistant prepares the referral to the agency in the template with the client's recorded consent
Assistant checks the final referral: what is asked, the client details shared, the recorded consent and the agency
Assistant sends the checked referral to the agency
Assistant phones the client later to check they got help

tasks.design: A search over the team's maintained social map in {DOCS} returns matching services with conditions and contact details, quoted from the entries, never generated advice; the information sheet prints from the chosen entries. Referrals use a template with the client's consent recorded, and a follow-up reminder is set; listening and explaining stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service information was scattered over websites, folders and colleagues' memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable records apps make a maintained social map practical.
tasks.still_hard: The social map is only as good as its upkeep; referrals carry sensitive data.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the service that fits this person and making the warm handover.

ambition.what: Every referral followed up to see whether the client actually got help.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; searching and sheets shrink.

reach.learn: Whether one shared social map serves both roles.

evidence.claim: Referral information is best delivered from a maintained social map, quoted rather than generated.
Health data is special-category data under the GDPR.
Municipalities and providers exchange care referrals through national message standards.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client's question to follow-up; the service itself is outside.
Input contract: social map entries kept by the team's information officer; client consent for referral recorded by the assistant; fallback is searching by hand.
Information officer and agency time is outside the assistant's savings.
Listening, explaining and the checks before the sheet and referral go out do not change. s6 keeps 85 because the follow-up call stays; the reminder removes keeping a call list.
unknowns: Whether the team keeps a social map today.
research_questions: How many referred clients actually reach the service?

already_counted.description: Assistant checks that found services fit the client.

incremental.description: Assistant reports outdated social map entries.
Information officer keeps the social map current.

approvals.approved_version: The referral with its request and the client details shared exactly as checked by the assistant in s5b, with the client's recorded consent, sent once to the named agency; any change needs a new check.
The information sheet with the chosen social map entries exactly as checked by the assistant in s4b, given once to that client; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the social map is not kept current, so assistants go back to searching websites and s2 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 70 (11.6); high: a current social map (21.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ask about money, food and care, build a budget, check possible allowances, advise on money and housekeeping, and help with forms.

steps.what: Assistant asks clients about their money, food and child care situation
Assistant makes a budget overview with the client on paper
Assistant checks which allowances and schemes the client may qualify for
Assistant advises on money management, food and housekeeping
Assistant helps fill in application forms prefilled from the client's data; by hand today
Assistant checks the completed application with the client: amounts, household details, attachments and the agency
Assistant submits the checked and signed application to the agency with the client's consent

tasks.design: A budget calculator in the case system ({OTHER}) uses standard household amounts and the client's income and fixed costs, and a rule-based check from published scheme criteria lists allowances the client may qualify for, as an indication only. Application forms are pre-filled from the client's data with consent; the conversation and advice stay with the assistant, and every eligibility decision stays with the agency.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budgets were drawn up on paper and scheme criteria looked up one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Budget calculators and rule-based scheme checks are plain code on published criteria.
tasks.still_hard: Debt and shame make the conversation hard; criteria change and must be kept current.
tasks.human_edge: Helping someone face their money situation without judgement.

ambition.what: Households who never asked for help get a full check of schemes they may qualify for at the first visit.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; arithmetic and look-ups shrink.

reach.learn: Whether the same calculator feeds their plans.

evidence.claim: Forms and budgets are prefilled forms and a budget calculator: deterministic code.
AI that decides eligibility for public assistance is high-risk; a rule-based indication without AI is not.
No eligibility decision may be based solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the household talk to forms filled; decisions by agencies are outside.
Input contract: standard household amounts and scheme criteria kept by the team leader from public sources; client data entered with consent; fallback is paper.
The scheme check is an indication; the agency decides.
Conversations, advice and the check of each application with the client do not change. s2 keeps 60 because entering income and costs with the client stays; the calculation goes.
unknowns: How many clients need budget help per month.
research_questions: Do clients claim more of the schemes they qualify for after the check?

already_counted.description: Assistant checks the indicated schemes against the client's situation.

incremental.description: Assistant reports schemes the check misses.
Team leader keeps standard amounts and criteria current.

approvals.approved_version: The application with amounts, household details and attachments exactly as checked with the client in s5b and signed by the client, submitted once to the named agency; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: clients with complex debt, where amounts must be gathered and forms rarely prefill, so s2 and s5 keep 80 (13.6); high: calculator and prefilled forms as designed (20.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run daily group activities, keep house rules, write the shift report on residents and hand over.

steps.what: Assistant oversees day-to-day group activities of residents
Assistant keeps watch on safety and house rules among residents
Assistant writes the shift report on each resident in free text
Assistant hands over to the next shift

tasks.design: Nothing changes in this task. The shift report on each resident is a first record of what the assistant saw; quick fields would replace a pen with a tap, so no time is counted. Running activities, keeping rules and the handover stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: None; the shift report is a first record of what the assistant saw.
tasks.still_hard: Group work with residents is people work; quick fields must not hide nuance.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a group of residents together and calm through the day.

evidence.claim: Dictation in care record systems turns spoken notes into structured reports for elder, disability and mental health care.
Health data is special-category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: one shift from activities to handover; care planning is outside.
The shift report keeps its full time: it is a first record of observations.
All steps keep their full time.
No dictation is used in this design.
research_questions: Do quick fields keep reports useful for care planning?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step changes: the shift report is a first record and group work stays in person, so low and high are 0.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The assistant keeps interviews, advice and group work; typing reports, searching services and budgets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant who follows up every referral and leaves no household without a check of what it may claim.
